column1: # Game profile of Bastion (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0). Plays on the Mac (logos, title, main menu, a new game into The Rippling Walls at 60 fps with music)
# Supergiant Games' C# engine on MonoGame 3.0 (Microsoft.Xna.Framework over NVN) compiled into main, XACT sound banks (.xgs / .xsb / .xwb) through the audio renderer, SDK 5.4.0.
# The shaders are MonoGame effects of MGFX version 5, each shader a whole GLSLC output: 24 in Content/Effects/*.xnb and 5 MonoGame stock effects in Resources/*.dx11.mgfxo
# (shader_split.py mgfx_effect). The provisional profile's guesses held: no key needed changing

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: it sets a heap of the application pool − used memory and allocates from it.
# The block is 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region
# the NPDM declares no system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon
# used memory for the rewritten modules (the NSP script's figure; main alone is 58 MB with its bss before the rewrite), more than the default 64 MB
